verdict.label: Light review
verdict.summary: You can test Slack OAuth immediately with your own account and Composio-managed apps, or register a custom Slack app with straightforward redirect configuration.

composioFit.summary: Composio provides a fully managed OAuth app for Slack by default, meaning you can skip registering your own app unless you need custom branding, dedicated rate limits, or custom scopes.
whyOwnApp: You need your own product branding and app name on the OAuth consent screen.
You need custom scopes not included in Composio's default set.
You are hitting shared provider rate limits and need a dedicated quota.
You are connecting to a custom instance or GovSlack.

phases.name: Create Slack App
steps: Go to Slack app management and create a new Slack app.
Configure OAuth & Permissions and add your redirect URI.
phases.handoff: Provide your Client ID and Client Secret to Composio.

phases.name: Configure Redirect URI and Scopes
steps: Add the Composio redirect URI in your app settings under OAuth & Permissions.
Ensure the redirect URI uses HTTPS.

phases.name: Test Connection
steps: Initiate the OAuth flow using the authorize URL with your client_id and required scopes.
Approve the scopes in your Slack workspace.

redirectRules.rule: The redirect_uri must use HTTPS and cannot contain an anchor (#).
Your redirect_uri must match or be a subdirectory of a Redirect URL configured under App Management.

blockers.cause: Multiple Redirect URLs are configured in App Management, but the redirect_uri parameter was omitted or did not match the value sent in the Access step.
blockers.fix: Include the redirect_uri parameter in both the Authorize and Access steps with the exact same value.
blockers.fallback: Use a single configured redirect URL in App Management.

blockers.symptom: API returns an error when passing access tokens in query strings
blockers.cause: Apps created after February 24, 2021 are prohibited from sending tokens as query parameters.
blockers.fix: Send access tokens in the HTTP Authorization header as a Bearer token or as a POST body parameter.
blockers.fallback: Use Slack's official SDK or libraries which handle token transport automatically.

blockers.cause: Attempting to combine Sign in with Slack (SIWS) user scopes with non-Sign in with Slack scopes in the same OAuth flow.
blockers.fix: Request each set of scopes in a separate OAuth flow.
blockers.fallback: Separate authentication flows for user sign-in and app installation.

checklist.text: Decide whether to use Composio-managed Slack auth or register a custom Slack app.
Create a new Slack app in the Slack App Management console if using custom auth.
Configure an HTTPS redirect URI under OAuth & Permissions.
Copy Client ID and Client Secret into the Composio dashboard auth config.
Construct the OAuth authorize URL with your required bot or user scopes.
Test the OAuth flow and complete the temporary authorization code exchange.

uncertainties: Exact turnaround times for Slack Marketplace app reviews are not explicitly documented in the provided excerpts.
Specific rate limit numbers for custom non-Marketplace tiers beyond general descriptions are not fully detailed.

claims.text: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Slack.
You can create a custom auth config for branding, scopes, rate limits, polling intervals, or custom instances.
claims.quote: You can still create a custom auth config for branding, scopes, rate limits, polling intervals, or custom instances.

claims.text: Slack apps are installed with a v2 OAuth 2.0 flow.
claims.quote: Slack apps are installed with a v2 OAuth 2.0 flow.

claims.text: Your app only has to worry about three steps to make OAuth work: requesting scopes, waiting for a user to give their approval, and exchanging a temporary authorization code for an access token.
claims.quote: your app really only has to worry about three steps to make OAuth work: requesting scopes, waiting for a user to give their approval, and exchanging a temporary authorization code for an access token.

claims.text: To request scopes, redirect Slack users to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize.
claims.quote: To request scopes, redirect Slack users to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize .

claims.text: Include both your app's client ID and a comma-separated list of scopes, such as scope=incoming-webhook,commands.
claims.quote: Include both your app's client ID, which is found in the App Management page, and a comma-separated list of scopes, such as: scope=incoming-webhook,commands .

claims.text: If you have specific need for a user token, provide a user_scope parameter with requested user scopes.
